content: Maraviroc is indicated for use in combination with other antiretroviral agents specifically for the treatment of CCR5-tropic HIV-1 infection. It must be administered orally twice daily and always in combination with other antiretroviral medications. The recommended dosage of maraviroc varies depending on concomitant medications due to potential drug interactions. Maraviroc is not recommended for patients with dual/mixed-tropic or CXCR4-tropic HIV-1. It is also contraindicated when co-administered with certain medications, such as elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, as this combination constitutes a complete antiretroviral regimen and should not be used with additional antiretrovirals. St. John’s Wort decreases maraviroc levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and is contraindicated. Similarly, apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, reduces maraviroc levels and should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, therapeutic efficacy should be monitored, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. Antiretroviral therapies (ARTs) may interfere with the manufacturing of cellular therapies such as atidarsagene autotemcel and betibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month prior to cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period to ensure complete elimination. Carbamazepine decreases maraviroc levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and should be avoided or substituted. Ceritinib and cimetidine increase maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution or alternative therapy. Elivaldogene autotemcel requires discontinuation of ARTs at least one month before stem cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Enzalutamide decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction and should be avoided. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Fexinidazole, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, increases maraviroc levels and may heighten the risk of adverse effects. Idelalisib, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, should not be co-administered with maraviroc due to increased drug levels. Ivosidenib decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, and co-administration should be avoided. Lasmiditan increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, necessitating caution. Lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing may be affected by ARTs, requiring discontinuation at least one month before mobilization. Quinidine increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring caution. Rifabutin and rifampin decrease maraviroc levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating alternative therapy. Sotorasib decreases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein induction, requiring dosage adjustments if co-administration is unavoidable. Tepotinib increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating dose reduction of maraviroc if co-administered. Thioridazine levels are increased by maraviroc via CYP2D6 inhibition, and this combination is contraindicated. Tovorafenib decreases maraviroc levels via weak CYP3A4 induction, requiring monitoring for therapeutic efficacy. Tucatinib increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating dose reduction of maraviroc. Maraviroc and acebutolol co-administration increases the risk of orthostatic hypotension due to pharmacodynamic synergy, requiring caution. Aldesleukin, alfuzosin, aliskiren, amifostine, and amiloride similarly increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension when combined with maraviroc. Amiodarone increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring monitoring. Amitriptyline, amlodipine, and amoxapine increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension when co-administered with maraviroc. Amobarbital decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, necessitating caution. Apomorphine increases the risk of orthostatic hypotension when combined with maraviroc. Aprepitant increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring monitoring. Armodafinil decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, necessitating caution. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, requiring monitoring. Asenapine increases the risk of orthostatic hypotension when co-administered with maraviroc. Atazanavir increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring dose reduction of maraviroc to 150 mg twice daily. Atenolol increases the risk of orthostatic hypotension when combined with maraviroc. Atomoxetine levels are increased by maraviroc via CYP2D6 inhibition, requiring monitoring. Atorvastatin increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution. Avanafil and azilsartan increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension when co-administered with maraviroc. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens increase maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially increasing toxicity. Benazepril increases the risk of orthostatic hypotension when combined with maraviroc. Benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels are increased by maraviroc via CYP2D6 inhibition, requiring monitoring. Berotralstat increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating dose titration. Betaxolol and bisoprolol increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension when co-administered with maraviroc. Bosentan decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, requiring caution. Budesonide decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, necessitating monitoring. Bumetanide increases the risk of orthostatic hypotension when combined with maraviroc. Butabarbital and butalbital decrease maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, requiring caution. Candesartan and captopril increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension when co-administered with maraviroc. Carvedilol levels are increased by maraviroc via CYP2D6 inhibition, requiring monitoring. Cenobamate decreases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 induction, necessitating dose adjustment of maraviroc. Chloramphenicol increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring dose reduction of maraviroc to 150 mg twice daily. Chlorothiazide and chlorthalidone increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension when combined with maraviroc. Clarithromycin increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating dose reduction of maraviroc to 150 mg twice daily. Clevidipine increases the risk of hypotension when co-administered with maraviroc. Clomipramine levels are increased by maraviroc via CYP2D6 inhibition, requiring monitoring. Clotrimazole decreases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein induction, necessitating caution. Cobicistat increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring dose reduction of maraviroc to 150 mg twice daily. Conivaptan increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating caution.
